- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for volatility.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to avoid overshoot after positive sentiment spikes.  
- If sentiment shows strong mean-reversion signals (e.g., recent highs followed by negative sentiment), model tends to hold high forecasts; reduce by 3–7% for 2–4 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture long-term downward trend; if sentiment shows sustained negative trend, apply a 5–10% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 3–5 day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
